messages:
Alex M.: Quick post‑RFC checkin — we need an ops-friendly rollout plan for per-model kernel flags + fallback kernels. RFC covered tradeoffs; want a concrete plan for next week
Maya R.: +1. Suggest: 1) feature flag per model + kernel_version tag 2) traffic percentages 3) automated fallback to 'default-kernel' on latency/error spike
Kevin T.: Agree. Need guardrails: max latency increase 10% over baseline OR error rate >0.5% should trigger rollback (auto)
Sara L.: How do we compute baseline? per-model p95 over last 24h? also what about KV-cache compatibility across kernels?
Alex M.: Baseline = rolling 24h p95 with min reqs threshold (10k). KV-cache: fallback requires cache_compatible=true; otherwise expect cold-start warm-up and higher latency
deploy-bot: rollout started for model:gpt-redwood-1 kernel:v2-canary at 1%
Maya R.: Ops naming convention: runtime.kernel.{model}.v{N}.enabled & runtime.kernel.{model}.v{N}.fallback to keep flags discoverable
Kevin T.: Also add runtime.kernel.{model}.canary.window = 30m and runtime.kernel.{model}.canary.steps = [1,5,20,50,100]
Sara L.: Can we allow weighted routing by client tier? e.g., dedicated customers pinned to stable kernel while hosted traffic goes to canary
Alex M.: Yes — routing.policies supports: ["latency", "cost", "pinned", "fallback", "canary-weight"]. Policy evaluation order: pinned -> canary-weight -> fallback -> latency-based routing
Maya R.: Proposed canary sequence: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation windows and automated smoke checks (latency/error/semantic diffs)
Kevin T.: Smoke checks = check p50/p95, token error rate, tail latency regressions, and a small set of golden prompts for semantic drift (compute embedding similarity). Fail fast if thresholds exceeded
Sara L.: For semantic diffs we need deterministic prompts. Who owns those?
Alex M.: Research provides canonical eval sets; runtime triggers eval job and posts results to #evals and attaches metadata to rollout event
Kevin T.: Example rollout config snippet:
```yaml
model: gpt-redwood-1
kernels:
  - id: v2-canary
    enabled_flag: runtime.kernel.gpt-redwood-1.v2.enabled
    fallback: v1-stable
    cache_compatible: true
canary_policy:
  steps: [1,5,20,50,100]
  window: 1800 # seconds
  rollback_on:
    latency_pct_increase: 0.10
    error_rate: 0.005
    semantic_similarity_drop: 0.85
telemetry: [p50, p95, error_rate, semantic_similarity]
alerts:
  - channel: #incidents
    severity: high
    on: [rollback, threshold_exceeded]
```
Maya R.: Telemetry note — ensure per-flag metrics: requests_by_flag, p95_by_flag, errors_by_flag, semantic_delta_by_flag. Pin retention to 30d for quick rollbacks
runtime-oncall: +1 — we need alert runbooks updated. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kernel-rollout
Kevin T.: Rollback actions should be automated for critical thresholds (flip flag back and notify), but require manual confirm for non-critical (semantic drift) with a 15m hold window
Alex M.: Agree. Also require an audit event for each flag change (user, CID, reason) surfaced in console and logs
Maya R.: Who will own the automation? Suggest runtime-team + eng-sre for alerting hooks. I can take the automation PR for canary driver next sprint
Sara L.: I can own the KV-cache compatibility matrix and a gating test to run pre-rollout (small smoke job that exercises cache hits/misses)
Alex M.: Plan/timeline: 1) finalize flag naming and policy schema (this week) 2) implement canary driver + telemetry (next sprint) 3) create runbook + alerting (parallel) 4) dry-run on internal models -> public canary
Maya R.: I'll open a ticket with the schema and an example config (assign Kevin + Sara).
Kevin T.: I'll sketch the automation PR and smoke-check harness.
Sara L.: I'll draft cache-compat tests and add to the pre-rollout checklist.
deploy-bot: rollout succeeded to 1% for model:gpt-redwood-1 kernel:v2-canary (monitoring enabled)
Alex M.: Nice — when rolling to 5% please run the semantic-sample job and post results here
Maya R.: noted. tagging @runtime-oncall for monitoring during the 5% step :thumbsup:
runtime-oncall: I'll watch graphs and escalate if needed.
Alex M.: Thanks all. I'll update the RFC follow-up doc with the plan and link tickets.
Maya R.: LGTM from feature-flagging POV. :rocket:
Kevin T.: LGTM from infra.
Sara L.: LGTM for cache gating.
Alex M.: Closing — will file follow-ups and announce schedule in #eng-runtime tomorrow.
